html:
From the 1840s, Niuean converts and Samoan teachers of the London Missionary Society brought Christianity to Niue. By the 1860s a resident missionary had arrived and most of the island had joined the church.

The church grew into the Ekalesia Niue, the island's own Congregational church. Village life came to turn around its services, choirs and feasts, and pastors took a lead role beside the chiefs.

Missionaries also wrote Niuean down for the first time, for the Bible and hymn books. The church later shaped Niue's links with Samoa and with the Niuean community that settled in New Zealand.
